name: AutoTune
description: While traffic microsimulation is an important and widespread tool for transportation research and engineering, its validity requires effective calibration. The community develops novel calibration algorithms with an assumption that progress is being made, but lacks a common benchmark to gauge these advancements. Algorithms’ opacity, implementation complexity, or proprietary data can hinder comparison, reproducibility, and collaborative research. To address this gap, this work introduces AutoTune, an open-source, large-scale microsimulation calibration benchmark built with data from the I-24 MOTION testbed. It enables robust assessment of calibration methods by providing microscopic and macroscopic ground-truth data, open-source implementations of key methods, and integration with popular car-following datasets. AutoTune supports calibrating diverse parameter categories to recreate traffic phenomena. A case study is presented to demonstrate its utility on a scenario of interest. AutoTune is available at https://github.com/chickert/AutoTune.
